subject: Zenith commit: price backstop, MFN and ML-index clause
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenith-ai.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@zenith-ai.com
Date: 2026-09-12T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing for Hosted API — Proposed Commit & Price Lock

Neha / Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Zenith is preparing a 12-month consumption commit for hosted API usage (roughly $1.2M run‑rate; precise volumes in the attached spreadsheet). Two key commercial asks from procurement that we need your position on before legal drafts:

- Price lock: Zenith is asking for a firm price lock for the duration of the 12‑month commitment (no per‑token list price increases during the term).
- Rate protections: MFN (most-favored-nation) clause that ensures Zenith doesn’t pay more than any other customer for the same model/region during the term. Also want an annual CPI cap or an index tie that limits price escalations (they proposed referencing a compute/ML index).

We understand you have standard policies — curious what flexibility exists for a named strategic customer and what you’d need from procurement/legal to move forward (PO, SOW, redlines). Attaching our commitment workbook for reference.

Alex Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships | Zenith AI
alex.chen@zenith-ai.com
Attachment: Zenith_Commit_Plan.xlsx (xlsx)

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenith-ai.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for Hosted API — Proposed Commit & Price Lock

Alex — great to see the numbers, thanks for the workbook.

High level response so we can keep procurement moving: we’re open to a committed 12‑month program with a meaningful price credit ladder tied to consumption tiers, and to limiting list price increases for a portion of the term. That said, we don’t ship unrestricted MFN clauses — typically we scope MFN to comparable customers (same commit magnitude and model family) and exclude one-off promotional programs. For CPI/index caps, we can do a bounded escalation mechanism rather than an open-ended formula.

Proposed counter (quick summary):
- Commit: 12 months, tiered discounts at 50/200/500M tokens per month.
- Price lock: guarantee no list price increases for 9 months; months 10–12 are eligible for a transition notice and a capped adjustment up to X% (we’ll propose a cap).
- MFN: limited to customers with >= 75% of Zenith’s committed monthly volume and in the same region/model family.
- CPI/Index: accept an annual cap but suggest a 6% ceiling (we can explore tying to a public compute index if procurement prefers an index-linked formula).

I’ve attached an initial term sheet (RNW-TermSheet-ZNTH-v1.pdf) with the above spelled out for legal to review. Can you confirm procurement’s latest timing and whether they require a DocuSign route or will issue a PO once terms are agreed? Looping in Lauren on the discount approval path.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: RNW-TermSheet-ZNTH-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenith-ai.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@zenith-ai.com, maya.lin@zenith-ai.com
Date: 2026-09-13T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing for Hosted API — Proposed Commit & Price Lock

Neha — thanks for the quick turnaround and term sheet. A few points from our side after internal review:

1) MFN: Zenith needs an unconditional MFN across all hosted token pricing for the same model family and region for the 12‑month term. Restricting by volume disqualifies the protection we require.
2) Price lock: we want the full 12 months covered. Our budgeting runs on a fiscal year and we can’t accept a 9‑month window followed by a potential increase.
3) CPI/index: procurement suggested a model‑compute index cap rather than general CPI; they want a 3% annual cap tied to an agreed ML compute index because they expect model-level efficiencies to reduce costs over time.

If Redwood can meet 1 & 2, we can execute quickly and route PO + standard SOW. If you can’t, we’ll need to escalate to procurement/legal for a final review.

Procurement contact is procurement@zenith-ai.com — they expect a DocuSign link for the final term sheet and will attach a PO upon signature.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships | Zenith AI
Attachment: Zenith_Commit_Plan.xlsx (re-sent)

From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Zenith negotiation strategy (MFN / CPI / price lock)

Team — quick note on negotiation posture and approvals before I reply to Alex:

- MFN: push for a narrowed MFN by model family + region + commitment band. If they insist on unconditional MFN, propose a carve‑out for limited pilot/promotional programs and require them to identify comparable customers for the MFN to be triggered. This protects us from broad MFN claims.

- Price lock: offer 12 months at the committed unit price but add a graduated protection: full lock on list for months 1–9, guaranteed not to increase for 12 months unless major cloud cost shocks (define threshold), and if we must adjust in months 10–12, offer a one‑time credit to Zenith to offset the effective increase. This provides buyers certainty while giving us limited flexibility for true cost shocks.

- CPI / ML index: counter to their 3% ask with a 4% cap tied to a specific published compute index (we should propose the 'ML Compute Cost Index v1' and limit adjustments to once per 12‑month period).

- Legal / Procurement: recommend we prepare a redline that includes: MFN scope language, a definition of "model family", the shock threshold formula, and a one‑time rebate mechanism. Also prepare an addendum that permits us to fallback to a quantized/discounted variant of the model if supply/capacity issues occur (keeps service continuity).

I’ll draft the reply to Alex that accepts 12 months, offers the adjusted MFN scope and a 4% ML-index cap, and explains the staged price lock with the rebate mechanism. Lauren — can you sign off on the discount bands in the term sheet? If yes, I’ll send to Alex and copy legal for redlines/docuSign prep.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
